name.text: Course to steer for a required track

questiontext.text:
A ship must make good a track of \([[if test="is(Tk<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(Tk<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@Tk@}^\circ\). Its speed through the water is \({@v@}\) knots, and a current flows towards \([[if test="is(k<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(k<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@k@}^\circ\) at \({@u@}\) knots.

(a) Find the course to steer, as a bearing correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Find the ground speed, correct to 1 decimal place.

[[input:ans2]] knots [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Draw the track line from the start towards \([[if test="is(Tk<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(Tk<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@Tk@}^\circ\) and the current arrow from the start (\({@u@}\) knots towards \([[if test="is(k<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(k<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@k@}^\circ\)). The course arrow, of length \({@v@}\), goes from the tip of the current arrow to meet the track line. The angle between the track and the current is \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\).

(a) By the sine rule, \(\sin d = \dfrac{ {@u@} \sin {@abs(rel)@}^\circ}{ {@v@} }\), so \(d = {@dispdp(float(ad),3)@}^\circ\). Steer into the current, on the other side of the track from it: course \(= {@Tk@}^\circ [[if test="is(dd>0)"]]-[[else]]+[[/if]] {@dispdp(float(ad),1)@}^\circ = [[if test="is(r1(cs)<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(r1(cs)<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@dispdp(float(r1(cs)),1)@}^\circ\).

(b) Resolve along the track: ground speed \(= {@v@} \cos {@dispdp(float(ad),1)@}^\circ + {@u@} \cos {@abs(rel)@}^\circ = {@dispdp(float(gs),3)@} \approx {@dispdp(r1(gs),1)@}\) knots.

questionnote.text: T={@Tk@}, v={@v@}, u={@u@}, k={@k@}, cs={@dispdp(float(cs),2)@}, gs={@dispdp(float(gs),2)@}

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: course to steer

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (f, g): Find the course to steer and the ground speed for a ship to make good a required track in a current.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 2, Section F (F4 and Example 8) of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Mechanics 1 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2004: steering to make good a required direction; bearings, a ship in a current, new numbers.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Steer into the current, not with it: the current pushes towards \([[if test="is(k<99.95)"]]0[[/if]][[if test="is(k<9.95)"]]0[[/if]]{@k@}^\circ\), so point the ship \({@dispdp(float(ad),1)@}^\circ\) the other way from the track.

\(\sin d = \dfrac{ {@u@} }{ {@v@} }\) only when the current is at right angles to the track. Here the angle between the track and the current is \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\), so only part of the current pushes across the track: use the sine rule in the velocity triangle.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(yo=0)"]]Your course is the same as the track, so the current would carry the ship off it.[[else]]Your course is \({@dispdp(float(abs(yo)),1)@}^\circ\) [[if test="is(yo>0)"]]clockwise[[else]]anticlockwise[[/if]] of the track, which gives the ship \({@v@} \times \sin {@dispdp(float(abs(yo)),1)@}^\circ = {@dispdp(yx,2)@}\) knots across the track. [[if test="ysame"]]That is the side the current is already pushing towards.[[else]]That must exactly cancel the part of the current that pushes across the track.[[/if]][[/if]] Use the sine rule in the velocity triangle, and steer on the side away from the current.

feedbackvariables.text: yh: is(abs(rel)<90); yb: if yh then is(ans2<=v) else is(ans2>=v);

truefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(abs(ans2-gs)>0.0501)"]]

Accepted, but your answer is a little away from the exact value because you used a rounded answer from (a). In later parts, keep the unrounded value from your calculator.

[[/if]]
\({@v@}\) knots is the speed through the water; the ground speed is along the track.
\(\sqrt{ {@v@}^2 - {@u@}^2}\) works only when the current is at right angles to the track. Resolve along the track instead.
Speeds subtract only when the current flows straight against the ship. Add the velocities as arrows.
Speeds add only when the current flows the same way as the ship. Add the velocities as arrows.

falsefeedback.text: The current flows at \({@abs(rel)@}^\circ\) to the track, so it [[if test="yh"]]helps the ship along the track: the ground speed must be more than \({@v@}\) knots[[else]]holds the ship back: the ground speed must be less than \({@v@}\) knots[[/if]][[if test="yb"]], and yours is not[[/if]]. Find the part of each velocity that lies along the track and add the two parts, or use the sine rule in the triangle.
